name: Analytics (Data Warehouse)
description: Business domain covering the AdventureWorks data warehouse: the dimensional model of facts (measurable events such as sales) and dimensions (the context they are analysed by, such as date, product and customer) built for reporting and data mining. Definitions in this domain are inferred from table and column names, because the warehouse carries no documentation.

name: Human Resources
description: Business domain covering the people who work for Adventure Works Cycles: employees, the departments and shifts they work in, their pay, and the job candidates who apply to join.

name: People and Contacts
description: Business domain covering the people and organizations Adventure Works deals with, and how to reach them: persons, business entities, addresses, email addresses, phone numbers and geographic locations. Employees, customers and vendors all draw on these shared concepts.

name: Production
description: Business domain covering the products Adventure Works Cycles sells or uses to manufacture what it sells: the product catalog and its classification, bills of materials, manufacturing work orders, inventory, prices and costs, and product documentation.

name: Purchasing
description: Business domain covering how Adventure Works Cycles buys parts and other goods from vendors: vendors, the products they supply, purchase orders and shipping methods.

name: Sales
description: Business domain covering how Adventure Works Cycles sells its bicycles, components and accessories to individual consumers and reseller stores: customers, orders, sales staff and territories, discounts, taxes, currencies and payment cards.

name: Dimension
description: A data warehouse table that describes the business context by which measures are analysed, such as date, product, customer, geography or sales territory. Dimension tables carry a surrogate key and, where they mirror an operational entity, the original business key as an alternate key. Definition inferred from table naming (Dim prefix) and structure.
